chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: The Charlie Straight offer he could not take
summary: He was offered a job with Charles Straight's band but his bandleader's contract and the club manager kept him, so he never recorded with Straight.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I was with that band and I was pretty busy with that band. I didn't get much time to hear it. But, I wanted to say I got an offer which was very flattering--- it was a very famous band called -- Charlie Straight --- he made a lot of records and I got an offer from him to join his band ---
While you were at the Rendezvous?
Yeah - while I was at the Rendezvous--- and I got - it was another question--- I couldn't get off to go --
Because you were tied up with---

Because I was with Ed and Fogarty said the same thing the other guy did -- he said -- we run a nice place here and you've been here a lot of times now -- you can't walk out on your contract--- I mean, it wasn't my contract; it was Eddie's contract.

And, you know, I had a perfect right to give two weeks notice, but he wouldn't hear of that. He said, as long as this band is here, you'll stay in the band. So, it wasn't--- I didn't go with Charlie Straight and, yet, people have said to this day, that I made records with Charlie Straight ---- somebody must have played just like me -- of course, I haven't heard it but everybody thinks it's me.
No, I didn't. I never made a record with him.
